steps.content: Ting-a-ling... ting-a-ling...

steps.speaker: Nino
steps.content: Look... look over there...
Nino tightens her grip and points at the shop window ahead of you.
A lonely table with a phone had suddenly appeared in the middle of the empty shop.
Your reflections and the phone form a perfect picture in the window... the phone appears right between you two.

steps.speaker: Nino
steps.content: It... it just keeps ringing. What should we do? Should we answer it? How would we answer it? What if we don't answer? Ahhh?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Don't panic. Let me try.
Staring at the phone's reflection, you reach out to the space between you two and make a motion of picking up the receiver.
The moment you "pick up the receiver", the ringing stops.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: ...Hello?

steps.speaker: Familiar Female Voice
steps.content: Hello there, my darlings~

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: What exactly are you trying to do? Steal people's voices?

steps.speaker: Familiar Female Voice
steps.content: Hehehe, I was just joking with you. You don't like this strange world, do you? You hate the voices here, right? Me too. I wish it could return to normal~

steps.speaker: Familiar Female Voice
steps.content: But it can't be helped. The world has lost its most important and precious voice, its one true voice. Terrible noises have taken over everything. That's why it's like this...

options: That's why you need my help?
Enough with this nonsense. What are you really trying to do?

steps.speaker: Familiar Female Voice
steps.content: Help me out! If you find that voice, I'll let you leave this place. How does that sound?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I don't believe a word you're saying.

steps.speaker: Familiar Female Voice
steps.content: Hahaha, you will help me. You want to leave this place. You hate it here, too.

steps.speaker: Familiar Female Voice
steps.content: Go find that lost voice. It's close to you. You'll definitely find it... I'll be counting on you.
Before you can voice your doubts, the "Call at 3 AM" has already hung up.
The table in the display window gets covered in dust the moment the call ends. That's when you realize that the phone didn't even have a telephone line.
This sort of thing is beyond what you can handle, and it is making you a bit irritated. You force yourself to calm down and focus on analyzing the situation.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: ...She can already control objects and sounds in the world, and even influence ordinary people who enter...

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: These are already S-Class powers. No matter what... I have to take the culprit away...

steps.speaker: Nino
steps.content: Though I don't know what you're talking about, I support you taking the culprit away...

steps.speaker: Nino
steps.content: So what should we do now... uhh...

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: ...Call me ${PlayerName}, or if you prefer, you can call me Chief.

steps.speaker: Nino
steps.content: Huh? Chief? You're a bigwig with a proper title?!
You look at Nino, somewhat speechless. Just a few minutes ago, she was scared and surprised about how you could adapt to this world so quickly. But in reality, she is an eccentric one herself.
You suddenly understand why that female ghost wants her voice: she always speaks her mind freely. Controlling someone like her must bring a sense of achievement.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: No time to think about that now. Better think about how to deal with these "voice thefts." She just said that she won't take all the voices at once.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: And the way she takes them is by using those strange creatures, who guide and trick us into saying those weird words...
You recall those strange words. They were all negative comments. Who were they meant for?
For us? For the fellows with the weird heads? Or... for the female ghost?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Anyway, we need to come up with a plan so that every time this radio station broadcasts, we can survive without saying a word...

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Otherwise, if we really lose our voices, we won't be able to speak up and refuse the "demands" of those strange people.

steps.speaker: Nino
steps.content: Why do we have to assume that we will lose our voices... And isn't that a bit hard to accomplish?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I'm just used to preparing for the worst-case scenarios.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: It's always better to have several plans... My adjutant always says that.
You take out your comms device, which hasn't mutated to suit this world since you've arrived. It's still out of power, becoming a burden on you.

options: Did you bring a comms device with you?

steps.speaker: Nino
steps.content: A comms device?

steps.speaker: Nino
steps.content: Yeah, I did. But I can't turn it on. Maybe it's because I fell on it.
Nino takes out her comms device, which is adorned by a string of clinking charms that looks almost heavier than the device itself.
She tries to turn it on, but the screen remains dark, showing no response.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Then... recording a voice message to loop playback probably won't work...
In this world, anything related to sound seems to carry a hint of eeriness.
A series of strange, intermittent sounds attracts your attention and interrupts your thoughts.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: That voice... sounds a bit like the "Call at 3 AM"?
"Hel...Hello... Welcome to Call... at 3 AM... Eh..."
It's a record store. The strange voice you hear is coming intermittently from inside. It sounds like the opening lines of that radio show.
But you notice that all the lines containing words like "no", "refuse", "resist", have all been censored, unable to be spoken.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: That record store is a bit strange. Let's go check it out. If all else fails, we might be able to get some words from the lyrics to get by.
